newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end up strongly in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end up strongly in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher in a quiet bounce from Friday's losses.
Traders said a strong dollar gave short debt position holders a reason to cover their positions after steep losses Friday and before a quiet week.

"It was shortcovering and a little technical bounce," said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED and F Man. He noted that June T-bonds nudged up toward resistance at 107-24/32 to 26/43 but fell short of there.
"There was no real news to really speak of except the dollar was strong," Pullen said. "That gave some comfort."
June T-bonds popped back toward session highs in the last minutes of trade, but trading overall was quiet, traders said.
"The slight bid to the market right on the close might suggest we try to test some resistance tomorrow," Pullen added.

Others agreed, saying the market could drift higher as shortcovering continues amid the dearth of fresh fundamental data this week. The economic line-up is rather slim until Friday's retail sales and producer price index.
Still, the overall tone is bearish, traders said.
"Basically, it looks like only a bear bounce at this point," Pullen said.

A T-bond futures trader said he expected to take out last Friday's high of 107-26/32 -- possibly by tomorrow. He said the tone is better, but noted that trading was very quiet to start the week this week.
"There is a decent chance we can take out last week's high but until it proves otherwise you've got to think lower," he said.
Targets remained in the 106-00 and 105-00 handles.
"This definitely feels counter-trendish," one futures analyst said. He pegged support at the September 19 low of 106-22/32 and at 105-20/32, the September 5 low.
"It really was more consolidation today and there weren't any real features from dealers or commercials," ED and F Man's Pullen said.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 20/32 at 107-20/32, 10-year notes rose 10/32 to 105-27/32, munis rose 12/32 to 112-3/32, September bills rose 0.025 bps to 94.300, and September Euros rose 0.030 to 93.725. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
